source: WHO Annual Cholera Cases and Deaths Surveillance
processing_notes: WHO annual cholera surveillance database shows zero cases reported for GNQ in all years prior to 2005. The 2005 epidemic (946 cases, 15 deaths) is the sole recorded event. Evidence type: Documented_Absence from WHO primary surveillance record. Note: BMC Public Health Cameroon study (doi:10.1186/s12889-025-23007-5) independently states 'Equatorial Guinea last reported in 2005' as a contextual aside, corroborating this absence.

source: The New Humanitarian 2005 Equatorial Guinea Cholera Report
processing_notes: Source states: '946 cases and 15 deaths' in Malabo 2005 epidemic; laboratory confirmation from Pasteur Institute Yaounde Cameroon. CFR 1.6% within expected range. Only documented cholera outbreak in GNQ history.

Source states: WHO AFRO consistently excludes GNQ from cholera-affected countries list. Evidence type: Documented_Absence confirmed by WHO exclusion and Lancet Global Health exclusion due to absence of sub-yearly data. Surveillance: operational IDSR framework.

Source states: WHO AFRO confirms GNQ cholera-free 2016-2020; maintained absence during global cholera resurgence. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Cross-validated: 4/6 neighboring countries also cholera-free.
Source states: WHO AFRO confirms GNQ NOT among 14 cholera-affected countries as of 2024. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. GNQ maintained cholera-free status through 2020-2023 global cholera surge.

source: WHO AFRO and ECDC Cholera Surveillance 2025-2026
processing_notes: Source states: WHO AFRO 2025 cholera bulletin lists the 19 African Region affected countries by name (Angola, Burundi, Comoros, DRC, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, South Sudan, Togo, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe) - Equatorial Guinea is NOT included. ECDC cholera worldwide overview (1 Jan 2026 to 26 May 2026) lists all countries reporting cases - GNQ not among them. Evidence type: Documented_Absence from comprehensive multi-country reporting tables with active countries explicitly listed. Surveillance system operational: GNQ National Epidemiological Surveillance System actively reported other notifiable diseases in 2025 and conducted WHO-supported EDO training in Malabo and Bata in 2026. Interpreted as 0 sCh cases (zero-transmission period).
